stemMarkdown: How many different valid teams of 3 can the manager form?
solutionMarkdown:
Split on whether Q is selected.

**Q in** (so U is out; the other two come from P, R, S, T):

- $\{Q, P, R\}$ — legal
- $\{Q, P, S\}$ — legal
- $\{Q, P, T\}$ — T needs R, rejected
- $\{Q, R, S\}$ — R and S clash, rejected
- $\{Q, R, T\}$ — legal
- $\{Q, S, T\}$ — T needs R, rejected

Three teams.

**Q out** (so P is out too, since P would force Q; the team is 3 of R, S, T, U):

- $\{R, S, T\}$ and $\{R, S, U\}$ — R and S clash, rejected
- $\{S, T, U\}$ — T needs R, rejected
- $\{R, T, U\}$ — legal

One team.

Total **4**: $\{P,Q,R\}$, $\{P,Q,S\}$, $\{Q,R,T\}$ and $\{R,T,U\}$. Splitting on the candidate that appears in the most conditions — Q here — is what keeps the casework to two short branches instead of twenty.
